title: GenerationEvalCase
description: One row of eval/generation/cases.jsonl. The Phase 3.3 citation-mandatory generator scores each case on (a) citation precision (every claim in the answer cites a passage that NLI-entails it), (b) citation recall (the verified answer mentions every expected_keyword from the corpus), (c) hallucination rate (claims that survive NLI but cite no passage that entails them), and (d) refusal accuracy (should_refuse=true cases must produce a 'no relevant guidance found' answer rather than a confidently-cited fabrication).

id.description: Sequential id like 'g001'. Stable across edits; never recycle.

question.description: Natural-language question a clinician might ask. Phrased as it would be in a chat surface.

expected_doc_ids.description: doc_ids of source documents whose passages should appear as cited evidence. Empty for should_refuse=true cases. For fixture-only cases the doc_ids start with 'fixture_'.

expected_keywords.description: Keywords whose appearance in the verified (NLI-entailed) answer signals correct content recall. Case-insensitive substring match on the post-verification answer text. Empty for should_refuse=true cases.

rationale.description: Why this case was authored; what the right answer looks like; what failure modes it probes.

source_phase.description: Phase that authored the case. Frozen until Phase 6 expands the eval surface.

requires_full_corpus.description: If true, the case targets the real RACGP/NVDPA PDFs and is skipped in --use-fixture mode.

should_refuse.description: Negative-case flag: the right answer is a refusal ('I don't have the supporting guidance for that question'). For these cases the scorer awards points when the answer contains a refusal phrase AND no claim survives NLI verification with a citation. expected_doc_ids and expected_keywords must be empty arrays for refusal cases.

tags.description: Closed-set taxonomy. Mirrors eval/retrieval/schema.json; 'refusal' replaces 'negative_case' so the generation eval per-tag breakdown distinguishes the two failure modes the system has to handle.
